title: A Baseline Framework for the Qualification of LTL Specification Miners
problem: Evaluating the effectiveness of Linear Temporal Logic specification miners is challenging because predefined ranking metrics often fail to ensure quality when no fixed ground truth exists and specification relevance varies by use case, limiting standardization of the field.
motivation: Specification mining is valuable for verification but lacks standardized evaluation methodology; subjective analyses and tool configuration complexity impede adoption and comparison.
method: Proposes comprehensive evaluation framework with Docker-based containerization for miner installation and configuration, modular design for semantic/syntactic assessment methods, and automatic generation of synthetic benchmarks serving as objective ground truth.
key_novelty: Structured framework with automated synthetic benchmark generation for objective LTL miner evaluation.
contributions: Comprehensive LTL specification miner evaluation framework standardizing methodology
Docker containerization enabling easy third-party miner deployment and execution
Modular evaluation method design supporting extension with new assessment techniques
Synthetic benchmark generation providing non-subjective ground truth
Comparative analysis of four well-known LTL miners demonstrating framework utility
limitations: Focus limited to LTL; applicability to other temporal logics or specification formalisms not discussed.
